get.summary: Reads a shape: a snapshot and change log of a collection and filter
get.description: where is a query v1 filter as JSON (optional; every document without it). offset -1 answers 307 to the first snapshot page snap.<S>.0 of head S, with the shape's handle. Snapshot pages hold at most 1000 documents or 1 MiB in id order (one document may exceed 1 MiB with framing, up to 8 MiB); the last one continues at log position S. A log position O returns the commits after O, at most 4096 of them and 1 MiB, grouped by commit offset; a document that is deleted or stops matching is a delete op, and a delete may name a document the client never received. handle is required unless offset is -1; a stale handle or an offset outside the available history answers 409 must_refetch with the current handle: discard the shape and restart at -1. live=true (log positions only) waits up to 20 seconds for a commit when O is the head, then returns no changes; send the TB-Shape-Cursor of the previous response as cursor; each response advances beyond that cursor, even within one time bucket. Snapshot pages and closed chunks have immutable bytes and stable ETags. Origin responses use private, max-age=0, must-revalidate so every reuse checks current authorization; every response varies on Authorization. Shared CDN caching requires authorization before every cache lookup and is not enabled by these headers. TB-Shape-Handle, TB-Shape-Next-Offset and TB-Shape-Up-To-Date mirror the body; If-None-Match with the ETag returns 304. Treat client state as consistent only when up_to_date is true. At capacity, requests return 429 shape_busy; filters whose canonical continuation URL cannot fit an 8 KiB request line return 414 uri_too_long before redirecting.

P is a JSON Pointer of object members (nested paths allowed) or "$id"; V is a JSON scalar. Ordered comparisons only match values of V's type and reject null; ne and nin also match missing members. sort has at most 4 {path, order} keys, then id; repeated paths retain only their first occurrence, and keys after the unique $id are omitted; encoded cursors are at most 1 MiB and cursor-producing string values are at most 64 KiB UTF-8 each, and the compact query plus continuation must fit the 4 MiB request limit (400 sort_requires_index beyond); values order missing < null < false < true < numbers < strings < arrays/objects. project keeps at most 64 paths with their parents; duplicate decoded paths and descendants covered by selected ancestors are copied only once, with case-sensitive member names. limit is 1 to 1000 (default 50); a page also stops at 8 MiB of JSON. cursor is the previous page's next_cursor and only works with the same filter, sort and project (400 invalid_cursor). count counts matches among at most 100000 documents (exact is false beyond, and value is a lower bound), on requests without a cursor. Queries and counts are interrupted at SQLite progress callbacks after 5 million VM instructions or a 5-second deadline (400 invalid_query, query too expensive). Cancellation also interrupts SQLite. A field sort requires at most 10000 live candidate documents and at most 8 MiB of candidate JSON, otherwise 400 sort_requires_index. lower and explain are not supported yet.

Fences and assertions see the state before the commit, other operations run in order, limits compare the counts after with their bound and fail only when the count grew past it. Failures write nothing and name the operation in error.op. A retry with the same id and byte-identical body answers the recorded response with TerraBase-Commit-Replayed: true; a different body under a committed id is 409 commit_id_reused. Document operations need the management service credential (403 with a ts-auth token). accept_invitation and decline_invitation use the access token's verified email (403 without one).
